newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal can sustain state deficit 3 pct/GDP-BoP.
newsitem.headline: Portugal can sustain state deficit 3 pct/GDP-BoP.

text.p: Portugal is capable of cutting its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product and sustaining this level without taking drastic steps such as raising taxes, Bank of Portugal governor Antonio de Sousa said.
"Three percent is sustainable," he told Reuters on the sidelines of a banking conference.

He said Portugal had steadily cut its budget deficit every year since 1993. The country is trying to cut the deficit to within three percent of GDP this year to meet targets for joining the European single currency, or euro, in 1999.
The government has forecast that it will cut the budget deficit to 2.9 percent this year from 4.0 percent in 1996.

"The downward trend in the budget deficit was not obtained via tax increases or big policy changes of any kind," De Sousa said. "The deficit has fallen by about one percentage point per year," he added.

When asked to comment on a press report this week about a plan to delay the entry of so-called "Club Med" countries to the euro, De Sousa reiterated that applicant countries must adhere to the terms of the Maastricht treaty.
"In the treaty the criteria that have to be met have been defined and so the treaty will be applied in this way," he said.
